audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Jethro, Zipporah and sons, testimony of deliverance, meal before Divine, delegation of judges, and sustainable leadership.

familiar.text: And Jethro, Moses’ father in law, came with his sons and his wife unto Moses into the wilderness, where he encamped at the mount of God:

familiar.text: And he said unto Moses, I thy father in law Jethro am come unto thee, and thy wife, and her two sons with her.

familiar.text: And Moses went out to meet his father in law, and did obeisance, and kissed him; and they asked each other of their welfare; and they came into the tent.

familiar.text: And Moses told his father in law all that the LORD had done unto Pharaoh and to the Egyptians for Israel’s sake, and all the travail that had come upon them by the way, and how the LORD delivered them.

familiar.text: And Jethro rejoiced for all the goodness which the LORD had done to Israel, whom he had delivered out of the hand of the Egyptians.

familiar.text: And Jethro said, Blessed be the LORD, who hath delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of Pharaoh, who hath delivered the people from under the hand of the Egyptians.

verses.restored: Now I know that YHWH is greater than all gods, because in the matter in which they acted arrogantly against them.

familiar.text: Now I know that the LORD is greater than all gods: for in the thing wherein they dealt proudly he was above them.

verses.restored: It happened next day Moses sat to judge the people, and people stood around Moses from morning until evening.

familiar.text: And it came to pass on the morrow, that Moses sat to judge the people: and the people stood by Moses from the morning unto the evening.

familiar.text: And when Moses’ father in law saw all that he did to the people, he said, What is this thing that thou doest to the people? why sittest thou thyself alone, and all the people stand by thee from morning unto even?

familiar.text: And Moses said unto his father in law, Because the people come unto me to enquire of God:

familiar.text: When they have a matter, they come unto me; and I judge between one and another, and I do make them know the statutes of God, and his laws.

familiar.text: And Moses’ father in law said unto him, The thing that thou doest is not good.

familiar.text: Thou wilt surely wear away, both thou, and this people that is with thee: for this thing is too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone.

familiar.text: So Moses hearkened to the voice of his father in law, and did all that he had said.

familiar.text: And they judged the people at all seasons: the hard causes they brought unto Moses, but every small matter they judged themselves.

translation_notes: Jethro is Midianite priest and gives true wisdom; preserve non-Israelite wisdom and hospitality.
Leadership sustainability is explicit: 'not good,' too heavy, you cannot do it alone.
Delegation requires capable, truth-grounded people who hate unjust gain.
Zipporah and sons re-enter the narrative; do not erase them.
safety_note: Exodus 18 supports distributed leadership, not charismatic bottlenecking. It is a major anti-burnout and anti-domination text.
